title: Brauer pullback along finite modifications of reduced curves
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $f:C	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a curve [def-sc-curves] which is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Let $Y$ be a scheme and $
u:Y	o C$ a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $V\subseteq C$ be a dense open such that $
u^{-1}(V)	o V$ is an isomorphism. Then canonical pullback
$$H^2(C_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf G_{m,C})\longrightarrow H^2(Y_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf G_{m,Y})$$
is injective [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-br]. The map is cohomology pullback to $
u^*\mathbf G_{m,C}$ followed by $
u^*\mathbf G_{m,C}	o\mathbf G_{m,Y}$. No smoothness, reducedness or connectedness is imposed on $Y$, and properness of $C$ is not required.

source.place: Proof, Step 2 (normalization), units sequence and its cokernel; proof text retained in the parent DAG node

proof.text: A finite morphism has closed image; the isomorphism over V puts V in this image, so density gives surjectivity. This persists after etale base change. A unit whose pullback is 1 differs from 1 by a function vanishing in every residue field. An etale scheme over reduced C is reduced, so this difference is zero. Thus G_m,C → ν_*G_m,Y is a monomorphism. Let Q be its cokernel. Over V the map is an isomorphism, so Q restricts to zero.

Finite type makes C Noetherian. Density of V implies it contains each generic point: if the closed complement contained one, it would contain its entire irreducible component and thus a nonempty open of C. Therefore Z=C minus V contains no generic point. In dimension at most one every non-generic point is closed (a strict specialization beyond it would produce a chain of length two). The closed-point closed subset Z is finite. Each residue field is a finite extension of k by finite type and the field form of the Nullstellensatz, hence equals algebraically closed k.

A sheaf supported on finitely many closed points with separably closed residue fields has vanishing positive-degree cohomology: on geometric stalks it is the direct sum of the pushforwards of its restrictions to these points; finite pushforward is exact and the point cohomology vanishes for every abelian coefficient sheaf. In particular H^1(C,Q)=0.

Apply the long exact cohomology sequence of 0 → G_m,C → ν_*G_m,Y → Q → 0. Since H^1(C,Q)=0, its H^2 map is injective. Exact finite pushforward identifies H^2(C,ν_*G_m,Y) with H^2(Y,G_m,Y). By adjunction and naturality of the edge map, this composite is the stated canonical pullback.
